newsitem.title: UK: UK orders First Atlantic Equities to stop trading.
newsitem.headline: UK orders First Atlantic Equities to stop trading.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Futures Auithority said on Friday that it had ordered a small London-based brokerage, First Atlantic Equities Ltd, to stop trading.
The SFA said in a statement that the company introduced British customers who wanted to buy U.S. and Canadian shares to North American brokers.
It said First Altlantic Equities had provided "false, misleading or inaccurate information" in order to win authorisation from the SFA in May 1996, and misrepresented the company's true ownership.
The SFA added the company "had no reasonable prospect of complying with the SFA's financial resource requirements."
An SFA spokesman said that First Atlantic Equities, which employs five people at offices in Regent Street, central London, had the right to appeal against the decision.
The SFA ordered all of First Atlantic Equities' business to be transferred to another firm.
